text:
ben: Quick follow-up on the CP separation RFC — thinking about tenant ingress boundary for private VPCs. TL;DR: leaning toward per-tenant private endpoints + minimal CP surface, but worried about ops & cert churn. Thoughts?

ashley: I prefer per-tenant private endpoint for isolation. Main worry is egress IP preservation for customers who do allowlists.

priya: Agree w/ Ashley on isolation. Ops overhead and certificate rotation across many endpoints is the real cost.

matt: FWIW another option is a regional shared ingress relay (peered gateway) + per-tenant routing/policy. Fewer endpoints to manage but bigger trust boundary and central egress IPs.

ben: Right — tradeoff is isolation vs operational scale. Which customers need strict isolation (enterprise) vs those who accept shared gateway?

natalie: Enterprise customers will push for isolated CP surfaces for audit/KMS reasons. They often require dedicated endpoints or dedicated capacity.

kai: Ops notes: per-tenant endpoints mean endpoint churn during rollouts. We need automated bootstrap: ephemeral certs, idempotent bootstrap, and an operator-friendly rotator. Could reuse the agent bootstrap flow.

ashley: Sketch of desired behavior: per-tenant private endpoint -> CP accepts MNID-scoped tokens and mTLS client certs. Fallback path: regional shared gateway with tenant tags for routing. Need a clear rollout plan.

ben: Implementation questions to resolve: 1) handshake flow (mTLS + token exchange? client cert issuance?), 2) route discovery (cross-account peering vs PrivateLink?), 3) egress IP handoff for allowlisted customers.

priya: For 1) I prefer mTLS + short-lived tokens. Avoid doing ACME per endpoint if possible. Suggest we mint client certs from CP CA and have an automated revoke flow.

matt: On 2) we should support both PrivateLink-style endpoints (AWS ENIs) and peering-based relays. PrivateLink is nicer for security but more expensive and sometimes limited by quota.

ben: Good point. For peering we get cheaper scale but more surface area to manage. PrivateLink gives isolation but higher per-connection cost.

kai: Operationally we need: automated endpoint lifecycle (create/update/delete), cert rotator, mapping service for tenant->endpoint, and e2e tests for failover to shared gateway. Also observability: trace propagation + per-tenant metrics.

ashley: Small handshake sketch (informal):
```
1. Endpoint created in tenant VPC (PrivateLink or peered ENI).
2. Agent connects to bootstrap endpoint, exchanges short token -> CP issues client cert.
3. mTLS established; control plane accepts MNID-scoped sessions only.
```
This avoids ACME in the data path.

priya: That looks good. Also we should limit token lifetime and require re-bootstrap on major policy changes. Add audit log entry for each bootstrap.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: controlplane-api v2 -> prod at 1805560000 (no downtime expected).

matt: Rollout idea: default new tenants to shared regional gateway (fast path), offer per-tenant endpoints as opt-in for enterprise, and auto-promote heavy tenants to private endpoints when they exceed a threshold.

ben: Action items: (1) spike: cost + ops runbook (kai, priya), (2) diagram the handshake & CBOR sequence (ashley), (3) runtime routing shim for fallback/shared gateway (matt). Sync Wed 11am.

ashley: +1. I'll start the sequence diagram and open a PR to the RFC repo with the handshake.

priya: I'll run rough cost comparisons (PrivateLink vs peering vs shared gateway) and list cert rotation options.

ben: Great — if anyone has objections or additions ping me. :thumbsup:
